hero.headline: Woman found shot in Vero Beach roadway dies; sheriff identifies person of interest as Matthew Allen Waggle
hero.teaser: A woman found with a gunshot wound in a Vero Beach roadway Sunday morning died at a hospital, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office has identified 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle as a person of interest in the homicide investigation.
hero.body:
A woman found with a gunshot wound in a Vero Beach roadway Sunday morning died at a hospital, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office has identified 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle as a person of interest in the homicide investigation. Deputies responded at 8:41 a.m. Sunday to 501 First Street after receiving a 911 call about a woman in the roadway and found her with an apparent gunshot wound. The woman was transported to a hospital where she was later pronounced dead.

Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said the victim and Waggle were in a relationship. Investigators believe Waggle may have been in the area around the time of the shooting and that the shooting happened near where the woman was found, in front of her residence. The sheriff's office has a domestic violence investigator working alongside homicide detectives.

Flowers said investigators believe Waggle has left the area and have expanded the search nationwide. The sheriff's office is warning anyone who sees Waggle not to approach him, as investigators believe it is possible he could harm himself or others. Authorities have not released the identity of the woman.

Anyone who witnessed the incident, was in the area of First Street Sunday morning, or has information that could help investigators is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Tips can also be submitted anonymously through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Melbourne man, 82, dies after single-vehicle crash on I-95 in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: An 82-year-old Melbourne man died Friday afternoon after a single-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 in St. Lucie County. The driver was pronounced dead at the scene after his 2002 Jee
cards.body:
An 82-year-old Melbourne man died Friday afternoon after a single-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 in St. Lucie County. The driver was pronounced dead at the scene after his 2002 Jeep Wrangler left the roadway and struck a tree in the median.

The crash was reported at 3:14 p.m. on August 14 on northbound Interstate 95 south of Gatlin Boulevard. According to investigators, the driver was traveling north in the inside lane when his Jeep Wrangler traveled off the roadway to the left and onto the paved left shoulder.

The vehicle continued in a northwest direction into the grass median, where the front end struck a tree. The Jeep came to rest in the median, facing west.

The driver was entrapped and sustained serious injuries. Investigators are still working to determine why the vehicle left the roadway. The crash remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Melbourne man, 82, dies after single-vehicle crash on I-95 in St. Lucie County
hero.teaser: An 82-year-old Melbourne man died Friday afternoon after a single-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 in St. Lucie County. The driver was pronounced dead at the scene after his 2002 Jee
hero.body:
An 82-year-old Melbourne man died Friday afternoon after a single-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 in St. Lucie County. The driver was pronounced dead at the scene after his 2002 Jeep Wrangler left the roadway and struck a tree in the median.

The crash was reported at 3:14 p.m. on August 14 on northbound Interstate 95 south of Gatlin Boulevard. According to investigators, the driver was traveling north in the inside lane when his Jeep Wrangler traveled off the roadway to the left and onto the paved left shoulder.

The vehicle continued in a northwest direction into the grass median, where the front end struck a tree. The Jeep came to rest in the median, facing west.

The driver was entrapped and sustained serious injuries. Investigators are still working to determine why the vehicle left the roadway. The crash remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

hero.headline: Woman found shot in Vero Beach roadway dies; sheriff identifies person of interest as Matthew Allen Waggle
hero.teaser: A woman found with a gunshot wound in a Vero Beach roadway Sunday morning died at a hospital, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office has identified 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle as a person of interest in the homicide investigation.
hero.body:
A woman found with a gunshot wound in a Vero Beach roadway Sunday morning died at a hospital, and the Indian River County Sheriff's Office has identified 33-year-old Matthew Allen Waggle as a person of interest in the homicide investigation. Deputies responded at 8:41 a.m. Sunday to 501 First Street after receiving a 911 call about a woman in the roadway and found her with an apparent gunshot wound. The woman was transported to a hospital where she was later pronounced dead.

Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers said the victim and Waggle were in a relationship. Investigators believe Waggle may have been in the area around the time of the shooting and that the shooting happened near where the woman was found, in front of her residence. The sheriff's office has a domestic violence investigator working alongside homicide detectives.

Flowers said investigators believe Waggle has left the area and have expanded the search nationwide. The sheriff's office is warning anyone who sees Waggle not to approach him, as investigators believe it is possible he could harm himself or others. Authorities have not released the identity of the woman.

Anyone who witnessed the incident, was in the area of First Street Sunday morning, or has information that could help investigators is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. Tips can also be submitted anonymously through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.
